meaning.name: Make an invoice with vatkit
meaning.purpose: The shop's invoicing, with a sale to invoice, ends with every figure the invoice shows, to the cent, written as the customer's member state writes it.
meaning.steps: 1. The invoicing has a sale to invoice: its lines, each a net price with its category or none, and the customer's member state. 2. For a sale to a business, the invoicing gives vatkit the customer's VAT number and takes it back as it is filed; a number out of its form is refused, and the invoice waits for one in its form. A8, R7 3. The invoicing gives vatkit the sale's lines and its member state, and takes for each rate, highest first, the net, the VAT computed once on the sum, and the gross. A5, R5 4. If a line's category has no reduced rate in that member state, the whole sale is refused; the invoicing corrects the category, or names none for the standard rate, and splits it again. A5, A1, R1 5. If a net price is a float or below zero, the sale is refused and no figure is given; a refund is invoiced as a credit of its own. A5, R8 6. Where the invoice shows one price with its VAT, the invoicing takes the VAT on its net, the gross from its net, or the net in its gross. A2, A3, A4, R2, R3, R4 7. The invoicing writes each amount as the member state writes it, and issues the invoice. A6, R6
meaning.user: the program that calls it, the shop's invoicing

meaning.name: Release a change of a rate
meaning.purpose: The maintainer, told that a member state changes a rate, ends with a release of vatkit that gives the new rate from its first day in force.
meaning.steps: 1. A member state sets a new rate from a later day; the Commission's notices tell the maintainer and the finance lead. 2. The maintainer changes the rate in vatkit, and the day its rates hold to the new rate's first day in force. B8 R10 3. The maintainer changes the tests that pin the old rate and runs them all; none is left skipped for the change. R10 4. The maintainer names the rate and its first day in the changelog, and publishes the release on that day, a minor version, since no function's name or what it takes changes. R10 5. From that day the invoicing asks the rate of that member state and is given the new one. A1, R1

meaning.name: Give the rate of a sale
meaning.statement: When a program asks for the rate of a sale in a member state, with a category or none, vatkit shall give that state's standard rate, or the reduced rate of the category.

meaning.says: Given DE and no category, when the rate is asked, then it is 0.19.
Given DE and books, when the rate is asked, then it is 0.07.
Given fr in small letters, when the rate is asked, then France's 0.20 is given.
Given EL, and given GR, when the rate is asked, then both give Greece's 0.24.
Given DK and books, Denmark having no reduced rate, when the rate is asked, then it is refused with "DK has no reduced rate for books", and no rate is given.
Given CH, when the rate is asked, then it is refused with "CH is not a member state of the EU".

meaning.name: Release each change of a rate on its first day
meaning.statement: When a member state changes a rate, vatkit shall carry the new rate in a release published on the rate's first day in force, whose changelog names the rate and that day.

meaning.says: Given Finland's standard rate becomes 25.5% from 1 January 2026, when the change is released, then a release published on 1 January 2026 gives 0.255 for FI, the release before it still 0.24, and its changelog says "Finland's standard rate is 25.5%, from 1 January 2026."
Given that release, when a program asks the day its rates hold, then it is 1 January 2026.
Given a release that carries no change of a rate, when it is published, then the day its rates hold stays as it was.

meaning.name: The rate on a past day
meaning.statement: When a program asks for the rate a member state charged on a past day, vatkit shall give the rate that was in force on that day.

meaning.name: Give the VAT on a net price
meaning.statement: When a program asks for the VAT on a net price in a member state, vatkit shall give the net times the rate of R1, to the cent, a half cent rounded up.

meaning.says: Given 100.00 in DE, when the VAT is asked, then it is 19.00.
Given 0.05 in DE, whose VAT is 0.0095, when the VAT is asked, then it is 0.01.
Given 0.02 in DE, whose VAT is 0.0038, when the VAT is asked, then it is 0.00.
Given a country, a category or an amount that R1 or R8 refuses, when the VAT is asked, then it is refused in the same words, and no VAT is given.

meaning.name: Give the gross from a net price
meaning.statement: When a program asks for the gross of a net price in a member state, vatkit shall give the net to the cent plus the VAT on it of R2.

meaning.says: Given 100 in FR, when the gross is asked, then it is 120.00.
Given 10.00 of books in DE, when the gross is asked, then it is 10.70.
Given a country, a category or an amount that R1 or R8 refuses, when the gross is asked, then it is refused in the same words.

meaning.name: Give the net in a gross price
meaning.statement: When a program asks for the net in a gross price in a member state, vatkit shall give the gross divided by one plus the rate, to the cent, so that the VAT in that price is the gross less the net.

meaning.says: Given 119.00 in DE, when the net is asked, then it is 100.00, and the VAT in the price is 19.00.
Given 119 of books in DE, when the net is asked, then it is 111.21.
Given 0.03 in DE, when the net is asked, then it is 0.03, and the VAT in the price is 0.00: the net and the VAT make the gross to the cent.
Given a country, a category or an amount that R1 or R8 refuses, when the net is asked, then it is refused in the same words.

meaning.name: Split a sale by rate
meaning.statement: When a program gives vatkit a sale's lines, each a net price with its category or none, and the sale's country, vatkit shall give for each rate, highest first and named as an invoice writes it, the sum of its lines, the VAT computed once on that sum, and the gross.

meaning.says: Given two lines of 10.00 and a line of books of 20.00 in DE, when the sale is split, then 19% holds a net of 20.00, a VAT of 3.80 and a gross of 23.80, and 7% a net of 20.00, a VAT of 1.40 and a gross of 21.40, in that order.
Given a hundred lines of 0.05 in DE, when the sale is split, then 19% holds a VAT of 0.95, computed once on 5.00, not 1.00 computed line by line.
Given a line of 100 in FI, when the sale is split, then its rate is named 25.5%.
Given a line whose category has no reduced rate in that country, when the sale is split, then the whole sale is refused as R1 says, and nothing is given.

meaning.name: Write an amount as its country writes it
meaning.statement: When a program asks for an amount written for a member state, vatkit shall write it to the cent with that country's marks for the thousands and the cents and the euro sign where that country puts it, and as €1,234.50 for any other country or none.

meaning.says: Given 1234.5 for DE, when it is written, then it reads 1.234,50 €; for AT, IT and ES the same.
Given 1234.5 for NL, when it is written, then it reads €1.234,50.
Given 1234.5 for FR, when it is written, then it reads 1 234,50 €, with a narrow space for the thousands.
Given 1234.5 for IE, for PL, or for no country, when it is written, then it reads €1,234.50.
Given 0.125 for DE, when it is written, then it reads 0,13 €.
Given an amount that R8 refuses, when it is written, then it is refused in the same words.

meaning.name: Check that a VAT number is in its form
meaning.statement: When a program gives vatkit a VAT number, vatkit shall give it back as it is filed, its two letters and what follows them with no spaces, dots or dashes, where it is in its member state's form, and refuse it where it is not.

meaning.says: Given de 123 456 789, when it is checked, then DE123456789 is given back.
Given DE12345, when it is checked, then it is refused with "DE12345 is not in the form of a DE VAT number".
Given EL123456789, when it is checked, then it is given back as it is, a Greek number in Greece's form.
Given DE1, when it is checked, then it is refused with "'DE1' is too short to be a VAT number".
Given CH123456789, when it is checked, then it is refused with "CH is not a member state of the EU".
Given PT12, a member state with no form here, when it is checked, then it is given back: only its two letters are checked.
Given any number in its form, when it is checked, then nothing says whether it is registered: that is VIES's to say.

meaning.name: Refuse what is not an amount
meaning.statement: If an amount given to vatkit is a float, is not a number, or is below zero, then vatkit shall refuse it as a bad amount, saying which amount and why, and give no figure.

meaning.says: Given 0.1 as a float, when its VAT is asked, then it is refused with "0.1: give a Decimal, a whole number or a string, never a float".
Given abc, when its VAT is asked, then it is refused with "'abc' is not an amount".
Given -1, when its VAT is asked, then it is refused with "'-1' is below zero: a refund is a sale of its own, written as a credit".
Given 0, when its VAT is asked, then it is taken, and the VAT is 0.00.
Given a program that catches a ValueError, when vatkit refuses anything, then the program catches it.

meaning.name: The same from the shell
meaning.statement: When a person runs vatkit vat, gross, net, rate or check at the shell, vatkit shall print the answer of R2, R3, R4, R1 or R7, an amount as its country writes it and a rate as a percent, and end with 0.

meaning.says: Given vatkit gross 100 DE, when it is run, then it prints 119,00 € and ends with 0.
Given vatkit net 119 DE --category books, when it is run, then it prints 111,21 €.
Given vatkit rate FI, when it is run, then it prints 25.5%; given vatkit rate DE --category books, it prints 7%.
Given vatkit check de123456789, when it is run, then it prints DE123456789.
Given vatkit vat 100 CH, when it is run, then it prints "vatkit: CH is not a member state of the EU" on the error stream, prints nothing else, and ends with 2.

meaning.assumptions: - The tax office's audit samples the invoices of a year the same way each year, so that G1's counts compare. To check: read the size and the period of the sample in the tax office's letter of the 2026 audit.
meaning.journey: 1. The shop's invoicing has a sale: its lines, each with a net price and a category or none, the customer's country and, for a business, its VAT number. 2. It checks that the VAT number is in its country's form, and asks for the sale split by rate: for each rate, the net, the VAT and the gross. 3. It writes each amount on the invoice as the customer's country writes it, and issues the invoice. 4. In the back office someone checks a figure or a VAT number at the shell when a customer asks. 5. A member state changes a rate; the maintainer hears of it, changes vatkit and releases it; until the release, every invoice to that country carries the old rate, and today that is where it goes wrong (E80).
meaning.name: vatkit
meaning.non-goals: - Whether a VAT number is registered: that is VIES's to say, and vatkit calls no other system (E34, E68, E84). - Countries outside the EU: the finance team does not want them now (E84). - The rate that held on a past day, to correct old invoices: asked for and left out, R11 (E85). - Writing the invoice itself: vatkit gives the figures, and the invoicing writes and issues the invoice.
meaning.problem: In the tax office's audit of 2024, 37 of the 4,100 invoices sampled had a VAT a few cents off the office's own figure, each corrected with a credit note; version 2.0 put that right, and the audit of 2025 found none of 3,900 (E79, E75, E76). A change of a rate still reaches the invoices late: Finland's rate changed on 1 January 2026, vatkit carried it from 12 January, and 214 invoices to Finland went out at the old rate, each corrected by hand (E71, E80). The finance team heard of that change from a customer, and vatkit's maintainer moves to another team at the end of the year, so what vatkit promises is written down nowhere but in its code (E78, E83).
meaning.summary: vatkit gives the VAT of a sale in the EU to the programs that make Voltline's invoices, and to the back office at the shell: the rate of each member state, the VAT, the gross and the net of a price, a sale split by rate as an invoice shows it, an amount written as its country writes it, and whether a VAT number is in its country's form. This specification says what it does and what it promises, function by function and command by command, so that whoever keeps it after its maintainer moves on keeps the same promises (E78). It is for invoices whose VAT is the tax office's figure to the cent, and that carry a change of a rate from the day it is in force.
meaning.users: The program that calls it: the shop's invoicing and the back office's programs, which ask vatkit for every rate, VAT and amount an invoice shows (U1). The person at the shell: the three people of the back office, who check a figure or a customer's VAT number by hand from the command line a few times a day (U2). The maintainer: who keeps vatkit, follows each change of a rate in the member states, and releases it (U3).
